sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Ουσάκ: ρε-μιb-φα-σολ-λα-σιb-ντο-ρε

sources.title: Ordoulidis, N. (2011). «The Greek Popular Modes», British Postgraduate Musicology 11, p. 7
sources.quote: the 2nd degree "sometimes sounds flat and sometimes natural, depending on whether the melody is ascending or descending"

sources.title: Ordoulidis, N. (2011). «The Greek Popular Modes», British Postgraduate Musicology 11, p. 4
sources.quote: Greek musicians call ousák what maqam theory calls kürdî (example: «Το βαπόρι απ' την Περσία»); the Greek Ουσάκ scale is the Turkish Kürdî, not the Turkish Uşşâk.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: 5) Δρόμος Γκιουρντί ή Καρσιγιάρ ή Καρσιγάρ ή Κατσιγάρ: ρε-μι-φα-σολ-λαb-σι-ντο-ρε (one entry covering both Γκιουρντί and Καρσιγάρ)

sources.title: Ordoulidis, N. (2011). «The Greek Popular Modes», British Postgraduate Musicology 11, pp. 2, 4
sources.quote: Greek dhrómos kiourdí "is considered to be something completely different" from maqam kürdî; the two main Greek method books (Paghiátis, Nikolópoulos) give different scales for it.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Χιτζάζ: ρε-μιb-φα#-σολ-λα-σιb-ντο-ρε, «Η-ΤΡ-Η-Τ-Η-Τ-Τ», «ο πιο συνηθισμένος δρόμος στο ρεμπέτικο»

sources.title: Ordoulidis, N. (2011). «The Greek Popular Modes», British Postgraduate Musicology 11, p. 12
sources.quote: "dhrómos hitzáz does correspond to maqam hicâz"

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Χιτζασκιάρ: Ρε-Ρε# Φα# σολ λα λα# ντο# ρε — «σπάνια χρησιμοποιείται μόνος του· συνήθως συνδυάζεται με Χιτζάζ»

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Ραστ: Ντο Ρε Μι Φα Σολ Λα Σι Ντο (on C, the white keys)

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Rast», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.explanation: In descending phrases acem (b7) replaces eviç (7), per the TDV description of the makam's seyir as recorded in the research; the data records b7 in the 'descending' field. The makam's 3rd and 7th are a comma below equal temperament, which 12-TET rounds up.

sources.title: Ordoulidis, N. (2011). «The Greek Popular Modes», British Postgraduate Musicology 11, n. xxxii
sources.quote: Greek musicians often use Ραστ as a synonym for Ματζόρε (the major scale).

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Σαμπάχ: ρε-μι-φα-σολb-λα-σιb-ντο-ντο# — «ο μόνος δρόμος που ξεκινά από Ρε και τελειώνει σε Ντο#»

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Sabâ», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.quote: The upper şehnaz is explicitly not a perfect octave above the tonic dügâh.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Νιαβέντ: Ρε -μι-φα-σολ#-λα -λα# -ντο#- ρε

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Neveser», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.quote: A Nikriz tetrachord on the tonic plus a Hicaz tetrachord on the 5th: a nihavend with a raised 4th, "a minor oriental scale". The Greek shape is Turkish Neveser, not Nihavend.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Νικρίζ: ντο-ρε-μιb-φα#-σολ-λα-σιb-ντο — «προέρχεται από το Χιτζάζ, παιγμένος από τη 7η βαθμίδα»

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Χουζάμ: ρε-μι#-φα#-σολ-λα-σιb-ντο#-ρε, «ΤΡ-Η-Η-Τ-Η-ΤΡ-Η»

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Hüzzam», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.quote: Hüzzam is built on segâh: its tonic itself is a neutral pitch, a koma-flat B, which 12-TET frets cannot play.

sources.title: Rembetiko forum, «Χουζάμ, Σεγκιάχ ή κάτι άλλο;»
sources.quote: Four competing step patterns for «Χουζάμ/Σεγκιάχ» are listed; a participant calls the naming "a broken telephone… reversed names for tempered modes".

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Πειραιώτικος: ρε-μιb-φα#-σολ#-λα-σιb-ντο-ρε, «ένα Χιτζάζ με αυξημένη την 4η»

sources.title: Rembetiko forum, «Πειραιώτικος δρόμος»
sources.quote: Search results give both «…Σι♭ Ντο# Ρε» and «…Σι♭ Ντο»: the 7th varies (b7 or 7). The b7 form published here is the most common textual definition.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Δρόμος Γκιουρντί ή Καρσιγιάρ ή Καρσιγάρ ή Κατσιγάρ: ρε-μι-φα-σολ-λαb-σι-ντο-ρε

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Karcığar», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.quote: Uşşak tetrachord on dügâh plus Hicaz pentachord on nevâ; tonic dügâh. The 2nd is Uşşak's neutral 2nd, which Greek sources round up to E natural.

sources.title: N. Katsikias, «Δρόμοι Μουσικής», Greek school-network teacher page
sources.quote: Σεγκιάχ: ρε-μι#-φα#-σολ-λα-σι-ντο#-ρε, «ΤΡ-Η-Η-Τ-Τ-Τ-Η»

sources.title: İ. H. Özkan, «Segâh», TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi
sources.quote: Segâh is built on the segâh fifth; its tonic is the koma-flat B, a neutral pitch 12-TET cannot play.

sources.title: Rembetiko forum, «Χουζάμ, Σεγκιάχ ή κάτι άλλο;»
sources.quote: The descending form «3Η-Η-Η-Τ-Τ-Η-Τ» (b7 on the way down) appears in the thread's list of competing patterns.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Major scale
sources.quote: Most commonly, the term "major scale" refers to the natural major scale (or Ionian mode), which is one of the most commonly used musical scales, especially in Western music. It is one of the diatonic scales.

sources.title: el.wikipedia: Κλίμακα (μουσική)
sources.quote: Αν παίξουμε τη μείζονα κλίμακα του Ντο… αυτό που κάνουμε στην πραγματικότητα είναι να παίζουμε μια σειρά από τόνους και ημιτόνια με μια συγκεκριμένη σειρά.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Minor scale
sources.quote: There are three common types of minor scales: the natural minor scale, the melodic minor scale, and the harmonic minor scale.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Minor scale
sources.quote: This modification became known as the harmonic minor scale. The configuration creates an augmented second between the sixth and seventh scale degrees.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Minor scale
sources.quote: There are three common types of minor scales: the natural minor scale, the melodic minor scale, and the harmonic minor scale.

sources.title: tonal (@tonaljs/scale-type), scale-type data
sources.explanation: tonal's 'melodic minor' (1P 2M 3m 4P 5P 6M 7M) is the ascending (jazz) form only. In classical practice the scale reverts to natural minor on the way down; that form is recorded in the 'descending' field.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mode (music)

sources.title: Wikipedia: Pentatonic scale
sources.quote: The major pentatonic scale may be thought of as a gapped or incomplete major scale, using scale tones 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 of the major scale.

sources.title: el.wikipedia: Κλίμακα (μουσική)
sources.quote: μια πεντατονική κλίμακα περιέχει πέντε νότες

sources.title: Wikipedia: Pentatonic scale
sources.quote: Although various hemitonic pentatonic scales might be called minor, the term is most commonly applied to the relative minor pentatonic derived from the major pentatonic, using scale tones 1, 3, 4, 5, and 7 of the natural minor scale.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Blues scale
sources.quote: The hexatonic, or six-note, blues scale consists of the minor pentatonic scale plus the ♭5th degree of the original heptatonic scale.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Blues scale
sources.quote: A blues scale is often formed by the addition of an out-of-key "blue note" to an existing scale, notably the flat fifth addition to the minor pentatonic scale or the addition of the minor third to a major pentatonic scale.
